speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) if he can provide a progress update on (i) the plan to second up to 20 public officers to interested Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) under the Local Enterprise and Association Development-Plus programme and (ii) the status of the $30 million that was set aside in Budget 2016 to support TACs to develop their capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Through LEAD+ projects, TACs can strengthen their leadership and secretariat teams, improve organisational processes, and deliver new and value-added services to their members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: The LEAD+ programme is an expansion of the existing LEAD programme, which supports TACs in implementing industry initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: We expect more TACs to be coming on board over the next few years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Efforts to second public officers to TACs are not new.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Over the past five years, SPRING has been active in seconding officers to TACs on a project basis, to drive implementation of key programmes, such as the small and medium enterprises (SME) Talent Programme and SME Centres.
